en: Let us scatter their blood like seed,
uncertainty_note: The opening word is provisionally read Үрөндөй; the verb may be a nearby form.

en: Let us strike at their people,
[Uncertain: They have made that land their camp,]
uncertainty_note: The middle words атан орук are difficult; translation follows the apparent sense of a settled camp.

en: Saying, ‘If you wish, a detachment of a thousand,’
uncertainty_note: The word миңдей is a provisional reading of the compact final phrase.

en: Let us overrun Tobochokon,
uncertainty_note: Тобочокон is treated as a proper name but its exact spelling is uncertain.

en: [Uncertain: Let us set the rolling host aflame,]
uncertainty_note: Both words are provisional visual readings; the English only gives a possible sense.

en: We shall deal with their people as we see fit,
uncertainty_note: The short final verb is legible as кылабыз, though the idiom depends on adjacent lines.

en: We shall plunder without leaving a soul and then rest.
[Uncertain: Let us despoil those who are broken,]
uncertainty_note: The opening form and final verb are difficult; both are retained as seen.

en: If the accursed enemy breaks apart,
uncertainty_note: каргы is a provisional reading, understood as an epithet for the enemy.

en: Let us make it one realm,
uncertainty_note: The compound дүйнөкү is visually uncertain; translation follows дүйнө, ‘world or realm.’

en: Among the people who raised their royal camp,
After taking counsel, we shall appoint a champion,
Of the Burut who poses as a hero,
One who would plunder everything,
uncertainty_note: The final word is provisionally read төөчү; its intended verb may differ.

en: Making a khan from among the Kalmyks,
Laying low whoever opposes us,
Let us make their land a fortress,
uncertainty_note: The first word could be a nearby form; коргон салалы is comparatively clear.

en: Rather than leave even one among the Burut,
uncertainty_note: The phrase бир ага турмак is provisional; translation follows its apparent contrastive sense.

en: [Uncertain: Let us take the land and learn their intent.]
uncertainty_note: The syntax of жери ага is unresolved; оюн алалык is read literally as ‘let us take or learn the intent.’

en: Learn the disposition they have,
uncertainty_note: чаргын is a provisional visual reading and may name their condition or disposition.

en: Learn their hidden ways from their backs.
uncertainty_note: кайып is visually plausible but the idiom is uncertain.

en: Their brave men and their marksmen,
Learn them again and again.
uncertainty_note: The repeated word is visually read кайтып, though кайдан is also possible.

en: Putting their very lives into it,
uncertainty_note: The case ending and final converb are faint but this is the closest reading.

en: Without revealing their inner secret,
They learn one another’s intent beforehand.
uncertainty_note: The final form is retained as written; the subject and aspect are inferred from context.

en: How many roads there are, how many cliffs,
The bounds of their barriers,
uncertainty_note: The final noun is provisionally read чегирин, ‘boundary.’

en: The mountain passes girded with barriers,
uncertainty_note: аркан is clear enough visually but may be a different modifying word; English conveys the apparent terrain sense.

en: The places they have bound fast,
uncertainty_note: Opening Боп may be part of a longer or differently spelled form.

en: Their great lords and their khans,
By name—
uncertainty_note: A short standalone manuscript baseline; its syntax continues into the following line.

en: [Uncertain: Distinguish what people they are called,]
uncertainty_note: The phrase делиптен заада кыл is difficult; translation gives the apparent instruction to identify them.

en: Of the souls accustomed to that land,
uncertainty_note: The first noun may be a nearby form; the remainder is comparatively clear.

en: Observe them carefully from afar.
Taking measure of how long the road is,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Come and range across this ground.
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Go out scouting and survey the land,
Keep watch and reconnoiter the country,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Let us see which way there is movement.
Take the measure of the army,
Stand ready again, comrades,
Heroes ready for the hunt,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Enter the battle without fleeing,
Fulfil the duty owed to the people,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Go today for the people of Beijing,
For the people and lives of the forty khans,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: For all of this,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: For the hero Khan Chyngteñir,
Who would die as a sacrifice,
If you go, do not stay behind—truth or falsehood,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: The mortal who was born has seen it.
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Behind him he has a splendid swift one,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: He has a champion complete in every way.
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: He stayed watching this closely,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: From him came my seven forefathers,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: The common Kyrgyz move in an uproar,
They saw the full extent of it all.
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Having seen it, make this known,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Its sovereign was wrathful,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: If so, break the roadward side,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: He had remained after seeing many things.
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: They are numerous, but have no sense,
They are a thriving Chinese people,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: If you sit and look upon their multitude,
They are black vermin beyond counting,

text: Ушул аз гана элге ээ болбой,
en: Unable to master even this small people,
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Your driving them has brought disgrace.
uncertainty_note: Completion-first reading is provisional because one or more cursive words or word boundaries are ambiguous in the scan.

en: Short of wit and without honor,
With no brave man to inspire awe,
With little pride and without honor,
Their heads are dark, their antlers forked,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: These seem to be a hostile people to me.
Without courage and without honor,
What sort of great creature has emerged?
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: Kakan-chyn, khan of forty in battle,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: This Beijing upon which light has fallen,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: Owes a debt of words to our father,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: Striking Aidarot against the people,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: There is our father's grievance in it.
My Kaldais, my commanders,
A pearl-stone fit to wear as a necklace,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: My warriors who stand dressed for battle,
My marksman reared for the letter's summons,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: My hero who was left childless,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: I joined what had not been joined,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: Having seen much, both great and evil,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: I asked the noblewomen.
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: After asking, I myself,
Burned and baked until I became an ember,
I mourned what had come for its sake.
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: I shall stand towering like a giant,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: I waited and asked for their chief,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: Neither eating food nor taking a meal,
I am wounded as though struck by a bullet,
My age has been overturned,
Thinking, I longed for many things.
In the fortress-gardens of Beijing,
In the time of my forefather, the radiant man,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: Many wondrous decrees are written,
uncertainty_note: Cursive letterforms or word division make this completion-first reading and translation provisional.

en: When I look upon the many decrees,
Dwelling in Alabotu,
A man who yielded to no one in combat!
